candidates.source_name: Internet Archive Wayback Machine CDX API — nbrm.mk /content/Platni sistemi/ archive
candidates.why_relevant: The Wayback CDX index returned dozens of archived NBRSM payment-systems artefacts, including the yearly 'Годишна информација за движењата во плаќањата во РМ/РСМ' PDFs for 2017, 2018, 2019, 2020 and Excel workbooks ('Годишен за веб МК.xlsx', 'Годишен извештај.xlsx'). Several of these live-site URLs have since 301'd/404'd, so the archive is the only route to superseded annual payment-statistics releases, older card/ATM/POS series and prior tariff/fee documents.
candidates.access_status: open, no auth; CDX API queryable programmatically
candidates.legal_status: Internet Archive terms; archived third-party content remains under original rights
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Enumerate snapshots via the CDX API (url=nbrm.mk*, filter on 'platni', 'karti', 'statistik', 'tarif'), then fetch each timestamped https://web.archive.org/web/<ts>/<url>; dedupe by digest; keep only statuscode 200 rows.
candidates.discovered_via_method: direct CDX API query (curl) after seed query on Wayback + nbrm.mk
queries_used: Wayback Machine nbrm.mk platni sistemi statistika archived
cdx/search/cdx url=nbrm.mk* filter=urlkey:.*platni.*
local_language_terms_used: Годишна информација за движењата во плаќањата

candidates.source_name: Wayback Machine — archived MK commercial bank tariff books and card fee pages (Komercijalna, Stopanska, NLB, Halkbank etc.)
candidates.why_relevant: Bank tariff books ('Тарифник за надоместоци', 'Одлука за тарифа') and card/POS fee pages are routinely overwritten with each revision; the archive is the only way to build a time series of MK card issuing/acquiring fees, ATM withdrawal charges and POS merchant service charges. Same CDX pattern that proved productive on nbrm.mk should apply per bank domain.
candidates.access_status: open; per-domain CDX enumeration required
candidates.legal_status: Internet Archive terms; original bank copyright on documents
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Run the CDX API per bank domain (kb.mk, stb.com.mk, nlb.mk, halkbank.mk, sparkasse.mk, ohridskabanka.mk, uni.com.mk, ptb.mk, silkroadbank.com.mk) with filters on 'tarif', 'karti', 'nadomest', 'pdf'; snapshot-diff to detect fee changes.
candidates.discovered_via_method: generalisation of the confirmed nbrm.mk CDX pattern to MK bank domains (pattern verified on nbrm.mk, not yet on bank domains)
queries_used: cdx/search/cdx url=<bank domain>* filter=urlkey:.*tarif.*

candidates.source_name: ECB Data Portal — Payments statistics (PAY dataset, card-based payment transactions incl. cash withdrawals)
candidates.why_relevant: Authoritative, methodologically harmonised comparator set for card payments, terminals (POS/ATM), transaction volumes and values across euro area and most non-euro EU members. North Macedonia is NOT an ECB reporter, so this is the benchmark layer used to normalise and interpret MK figures (e.g. cards per capita, POS density, transaction value per card) against BG/HR/RO/GR/SI peers. Bulk download and SDMX API available.
candidates.source_subtype: official statistical data portal / cross-country aggregator
candidates.access_status: open, free, no registration; HTTP 200 observed on the dataset page
candidates.legal_status: ECB open reuse with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: SDMX REST pull from the ECB Data Portal PAY dataflow (CSV/SDMX-ML) filtered to comparator reference areas; schedule semi-annually to follow the H1/H2 payments statistics releases.
candidates.discovered_via_method: web search then direct HTTP check
queries_used: ECB payments statistics data portal card payments number of terminals non-euro area countries

candidates.source_name: ECB Payments statistics methodological notes (definitions for card/terminal indicators)
candidates.why_relevant: Defines 'non-remote card payment', 'terminal', 'card with a payment function' etc. Needed to test whether NBRSM's MK definitions are comparable before any MK-vs-EU benchmark is asserted; prevents false conclusions from definitional mismatch.
candidates.access_status: open PDF
candidates.legal_status: ECB open reuse with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: One-off PDF fetch; re-check on each ECB methodology revision.
queries_used: ECB payments statistics data portal card payments number of terminals non-euro area countries

candidates.source_name: CEIC Data — North Macedonia Payment System database
candidates.why_relevant: CEIC normalises and re-publishes MK payment-system series (ATM counts/density, payment system indicators) with source attribution and long history, in a machine-readable, comparably-coded form. Useful as a cross-check on NBRSM/State Statistical Office figures and to spot revisions or discontinuities.
candidates.access_status: landing pages HTTP 200 in a plain curl but WebFetch received HTTP 403 (bot defence); full series behind paid subscription — treat as bot-defended-but-live, not dead
candidates.legal_status: proprietary, subscription licence; redistribution restricted
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual/licensed access only. If a subscription exists, use the CEIC API; otherwise record metadata (series names, source attribution, coverage span) from public landing pages for source-mapping purposes only, no bulk scraping.
queries_used: CEIC North Macedonia number of ATMs POS terminals payment cards statistics
candidates.observed_blocker: WebFetch returned HTTP 403 Forbidden on https://www.ceicdata.com/en/macedonia/payment-system; underlying series require paid CEIC subscription

candidates.source_name: Trading Economics — North Macedonia indicators (banking/money/financial block)
candidates.why_relevant: Fast, consistently-formatted mirror of MK macro-financial series (banks balance sheet, central bank balance sheet, deposit/lending rates, money supply, current account) with forecast overlays; handy for quick context around payments-market sizing and for change-detection when NBRSM publishes. Card/POS-specific series appear thin, so treat as macro context rather than payments-primary.
candidates.access_status: public pages HTTP 200; API and bulk export require paid plan
candidates.legal_status: proprietary; scraping prohibited by ToS, API licence required
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Licensed Trading Economics API if procured; otherwise manual reference only.
queries_used: Trading Economics North Macedonia banking payments indicators

candidates.source_name: Statista Market Insights — Banking / Digital Payments outlook, North Macedonia
candidates.why_relevant: Modelled market-size and forecast estimates for MK banking and digital payments (transaction value, users, ARPU). Statista's MK numbers are largely modelled rather than observed, so they are valuable as a commercially-circulated benchmark that clients and competitors cite — and as a signal of what the market believes — rather than as a primary measurement.
candidates.access_status: HTTP 200; headline figures visible, full outlook behind paid account
candidates.legal_status: proprietary, licence required for reuse/citation in deliverables
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Licensed account; capture methodology page alongside any figure so the modelled basis is always disclosed.
queries_used: Statista North Macedonia payment cards e-commerce digital payments market

candidates.source_name: IMF Financial Access Survey (FAS) — North Macedonia ATM/POS/branch series
candidates.why_relevant: The single most important cross-country normalised source for MK ATM and POS-terminal counts: FAS collects country-wide ATM numbers (search results indicate 1,041 MK ATMs in 2024 vs 1,023 in 2023) plus POS terminals disaggregated rural/urban, on an annual cycle with an October release. Because the underlying reporter is NBRSM, FAS also functions as an independent audit trail on MK-published counts.
candidates.access_status: open, free; bulk download and API
candidates.legal_status: IMF data terms, attribution required
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Annual pull of the FAS dataset filtered to MKD via the IMF data API or the DBnomics IMF/FAS mirror; diff year-on-year to catch back-revisions.
candidates.discovered_via_method: web search snowballed from ATM-count query
queries_used: IMF Financial Access Survey North Macedonia ATMs POS terminals data

candidates.source_name: DBnomics — IMF/FAS mirror (free machine-readable aggregator)
candidates.why_relevant: Free, open, API-first mirror of IMF FAS (and many other providers), which removes the licensing and bot-defence friction of CEIC/Trading Economics for the same underlying ATM/POS/access series. Best low-cost substitute for a paid aggregator.
candidates.access_status: open, HTTP 200 observed; documented free REST API
candidates.legal_status: open; upstream provider terms apply to the data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: DBnomics REST API (/v22/series/IMF/FAS?dimensions={"REF_AREA":["MK"]}) on an annual schedule; also scan DBnomics for other MK payment-relevant providers.
candidates.discovered_via_method: web search snowball from IMF FAS
queries_used: IMF Financial Access Survey North Macedonia ATMs POS terminals data

candidates.source_name: FRED (St. Louis Fed) — Geographical Outreach: Number of ATMs, Country Wide for Macedonia (MKDFCACNUM)
candidates.why_relevant: A named, stable series ID for MK country-wide ATM counts (FAS-derived), with a free API, CSV export and revision history. Ideal machine-collectable anchor for the ATM component of the cell.
candidates.access_status: curl returned 000 (connection/TLS timeout from this environment) — unverified, almost certainly live and bot-sensitive rather than dead; free API key required for the API
candidates.legal_status: free reuse subject to FRED terms and upstream IMF terms
candidates.suggested_collection_method: FRED API series/observations for MKDFCACNUM with an API key; also search FRED for sibling MKD* FAS series (POS terminals, branches).
queries_used: IMF Financial Access Survey North Macedonia ATMs POS terminals data
candidates.observed_blocker: curl -L returned HTTP code 000 (no response) from this environment; treated as hypothesis, not a dead link

candidates.source_name: World Bank Global Findex 2025 — North Macedonia microdata and country data
candidates.why_relevant: Only comparable demand-side source on MK adults' account ownership, card ownership and use, digital payment frequency, and cash reliance — the demand-side counterpart to NBRSM's supply-side card/POS counts, and the evidentiary basis for any 'cash usage' claim. 2025 wave covers 141 economies including MK, with downloadable microdata.
candidates.access_status: open catalogue; microdata download may require a free registered account and stated research purpose
candidates.legal_status: World Bank microdata licence (typically licensed/registered access), attribution required
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Register on the WB Microdata Library, download the MK subset and the 141-economy pooled file; also pull the headline indicators via the World Bank Indicators API.
queries_used: World Bank Global Findex 2025 North Macedonia

candidates.source_name: World Bank Open Data — North Macedonia, ATMs per 100,000 adults (FB.ATM.TOTL.P5) and related indicators
candidates.why_relevant: Free, API-accessible normalised MK ATM density series (long history; the CEIC restatement of it shows ~50.4 average 2005-2016, peak 60.7 in 2015, low 9.55 in 2005, ~67.15 in 2023) with directly comparable Western Balkan and EU values in the same call — the cheapest reliable comparator layer for the cell.
candidates.access_status: open, free API, no key
candidates.legal_status: CC BY 4.0 for most WB indicator data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: World Bank Indicators API: /v2/country/MKD;ALB;SRB;BIH;MNE;XKX;BGR;HRV/indicator/FB.ATM.TOTL.P5?format=json, annual refresh.
queries_used: CEIC North Macedonia number of ATMs POS terminals payment cards statistics

candidates.source_name: TheGlobalEconomy.com — North Macedonia ATM machines and financial indicators
candidates.why_relevant: Free, scrape-friendly re-presentation of WB/IMF MK banking and ATM indicators with ready-made country rankings; useful for quick peer-ranking checks and for spotting which MK indicators have been discontinued upstream. Derivative, so never a primary citation.
candidates.access_status: open, HTTP 200
candidates.legal_status: site terms; derivative of WB/IMF data
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Light HTML fetch for cross-checking only; always resolve back to the WB/IMF original.
queries_used: CEIC North Macedonia number of ATMs POS terminals payment cards statistics

candidates.source_name: World Bank — Western Balkans Payments Modernization Project (with RCC and CEFTA Secretariat, EC-funded)
candidates.why_relevant: The central regional programme on WB6 payments modernisation and integration, jointly run with RCC and the CEFTA Secretariat under the Common Regional Market agenda. Its diagnostics, country annexes and workshop materials are the richest regional source of MK payments benchmarking (cost of payments, interoperability, cross-border retail payments) and a snowball hub to further studies, consultants and named counterparts at NBRSM.
candidates.access_status: open, HTTP 200
candidates.legal_status: World Bank open access / CC BY for most publications
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the brief page and linked publications; mirror PDFs; snowball outbound links to RCC/CEFTA and to NBRSM press items.
candidates.discovered_via_method: seed query on RCC/CEFTA regional studies
queries_used: Regional Cooperation Council Western Balkans digital payments study CEFTA e-commerce report

candidates.source_name: Regional Cooperation Council (RCC) — Common Regional Market / Digital Transformation publications
candidates.why_relevant: RCC's CRM and Regional Digital Area workstreams generate comparative WB6 studies, action-plan monitoring reports and a documents library (crm_docs) that repeatedly touch e-commerce, digital payments and financial-services integration — a reliable snowball hub for MK-relevant regional evidence and for identifying which institutions hold the underlying data.
candidates.access_status: open, HTTP 200
candidates.legal_status: open publications, attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Crawl /crm_docs and the digital-economy/digital-transformation sections quarterly; filter PDFs on 'payment', 'e-commerce', 'financial', 'North Macedonia'.
queries_used: Regional Cooperation Council Western Balkans digital payments study CEFTA e-commerce report

candidates.source_name: CEFTA Secretariat — trade facilitation, digitalisation and e-commerce work programme
candidates.why_relevant: CEFTA's 2026 priorities centre on trade facilitation, digitalisation and reducing business barriers across WB6; its e-commerce and digital-payments strands (co-run with RCC and the World Bank) produce comparative studies and Joint Committee decisions that document MK-specific frictions in cross-border card and e-commerce payments.
candidates.access_status: open, HTTP 200
candidates.legal_status: open publications, attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Monitor the publications/documents and news sections; snowball to WB6 CIF and EC enlargement pages.
queries_used: Regional Cooperation Council Western Balkans digital payments study CEFTA e-commerce report

candidates.source_name: NBRSM press release — Western Balkans payment systems modernisation and regional interlinking (Banca d'Italia / ECB supported)
candidates.why_relevant: Found only via Macedonian-language search. Documents MK's participation in the ECB/Banca d'Italia-backed regional payment-system interlinking initiative — the MK-side entry point to a regional programme whose analytical outputs are the comparator material this cell needs. Also names the institutional counterparts to track.
candidates.source_subtype: central bank press release (pointer to regional programme)
candidates.access_status: public web page; nbrm.mk is known to bot-defend some /content/ PDFs (403s observed in the Wayback index)
candidates.legal_status: public official information
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Fetch the news item; follow to Banca d'Italia and ECB programme pages for the analytical annexes; archive a Wayback snapshot on capture.

candidates.source_name: Komercijalna Banka AD Skopje — quarterly investor presentations (PDF series)
candidates.why_relevant: Analyst-facing decks from the largest MK bank, published on a stable, guessable URL pattern (KB-PRESENTATION-DDMMYYYY[-ENG].pdf) each quarter. They carry market-share tables, card portfolio and channel/digital-banking indicators that are not in aggregate statistics, and constitute the commercial-analyst layer for MK. The predictable filename pattern makes them ideal for scheduled collection and for Wayback back-filling of withdrawn editions.
candidates.access_status: open PDFs
candidates.legal_status: public issuer disclosure; copyright of the bank, quote with attribution
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Quarterly fetch by URL pattern (both MK and ENG variants) plus Wayback CDX on kb.mk to recover superseded editions.
candidates.discovered_via_method: web search on rating/analyst coverage, snowballed to IR documents

candidates.why_relevant: Third-party commercial aggregator that normalises MK bank balance-sheet data into a ranked league table with market shares (e.g. Komercijalna ~192.60bn MKD / 20.61% and Stopanska ~157.22bn MKD / 16.82% for 2025 per its pages). Useful for fast market-structure framing that would otherwise require assembling individual bank reports.
candidates.access_status: HTTP 403 to automated curl (bot defence) — likely live in a normal browser; unverified
candidates.legal_status: proprietary site terms; scraping likely disallowed
candidates.suggested_collection_method: Manual browser reference only; verify every figure against NBRSM bank-system data before use.

candidates.source_name: bne IntelliNews — North Macedonia / Western Balkans financial-sector coverage and rating-action archive
candidates.why_relevant: Commercial regional business-intelligence outlet that reports rating actions on MK (e.g. the Fitch downgrade to 'BB' during the political crisis) and bank/payments developments in the Western Balkans, often summarising analyst reports that are otherwise paywalled. Serves as an early-warning and pointer layer into rating-agency and consultancy output.
candidates.access_status: part-open, part paywalled/subscription
candidates.legal_status: proprietary; licensed reuse only
candidates.suggested_collection_method: RSS/keyword monitoring on 'North Macedonia' + bank/payment terms; licensed subscription for full text.

candidates.source_name: Consultancy market-report vendors covering MK e-commerce and payments (Mordor Intelligence, ResearchAndMarkets, Verified Market Research)
candidates.why_relevant: These vendors publish MK-specific e-commerce/payments sizing and payment-method mix that circulate widely as the de facto commercial view (e.g. cards ~46% of 2024 e-commerce payment share with wallets growing fast; cash-on-delivery cited at ~70% of purchases; MK e-commerce ~USD 0.6bn in 2024). Their table-of-contents and sample pages are free and reveal which underlying MK sources they rely on — valuable as pointers even when the report itself is unaffordable.

candidates.why_relevant: PSP-facing country guides that enumerate MK acquirers, card schemes accepted, local payment methods, compliance requirements and fee norms — operational detail absent from official statistics. They also carry recent market claims (MK e-commerce EUR 213m in Q1 2025, cross-border shopping +32%, digital transactions +21% in 2024) that flag where to look for primary confirmation.
candidates.access_status: open
candidates.legal_status: site terms; treat as marketing content

candidates.why_relevant: Independent think-tank analysis of intra-Western-Balkans integration provides the analytical framing and comparator datasets used by EU institutions when assessing MK; free full-text PDFs make it a low-friction substitute for paywalled consultancy work.

candidates.source_name: NBRSM PxWeb statistical database (nbstat.nbrm.mk) — machine-readable series, MK/EN
candidates.why_relevant: Although NBRSM is a primary rather than aggregator source, the PxWeb instance is the machine-readable, API-addressable normalisation layer over MK central bank statistics and is the correct reconciliation target for every aggregator figure in this cell (CEIC, FAS, WB). PxWeb also exposes a stable table-path structure that can be diffed against Wayback snapshots to detect withdrawn or restructured tables.
candidates.source_subtype: official PxWeb statistical database with API
candidates.access_status: open; PxWeb JSON-stat API typically available at /api/v1/
candidates.legal_status: public official statistics, attribution

queries_used: Wayback Machine nbrm.mk platni sistemi statistika archived

negative_findings.description: No aggregator was found that carries a normalised North Macedonia POS-terminal count series in an openly accessible form. CEIC's MK payment-system pages surface ATM density (World Bank-sourced) but the searches surfaced no public MK POS-terminal or card-transaction-count series; the IMF FAS is the only cross-country source indicated to collect POS terminals, and even there the MK POS coverage was not directly observed.
negative_findings.result_summary: ATM counts are well covered by aggregators (WB, IMF FAS, FRED, CEIC); POS terminals and card transaction volumes are not, in any free aggregator found.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: POS terminal counts are the core Printec-relevant metric; if no aggregator carries them, the collection design must rely on NBRSM primary releases plus Wayback back-fill rather than on a comparator database.

negative_findings.description: North Macedonia does not report to ECB payments statistics (the ECB set covers euro area and most non-euro EU member states; MK is a candidate country, not an EU member).
negative_findings.result_summary: ECB PAY is usable only as a comparator/benchmark layer, never as a source of MK figures.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Prevents a costly and wrong assumption that MK data can be pulled from the ECB Data Portal; also means any MK-vs-EU comparison requires an explicit definitional bridge between NBRSM and ECB concepts.

negative_findings.description: No public rating-agency report on MK banks was located. Searches for Fitch/Moody's/S&P coverage of Komercijalna banka and Stopanska banka returned only secondary press (a bne IntelliNews item on a sovereign downgrade to 'BB') and the banks' own investor presentations, not agency documents.
negative_findings.result_summary: Rating-agency primary output on MK banks appears to be behind registration/subscription; only the sovereign rating narrative is publicly visible via press.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The rating-agency leg of this cell cannot be automated from open sources; it needs either free agency registration (Fitch and Moody's issue some press releases to registered users at no cost) or reliance on issuer IR decks and trade press as proxies.

negative_findings.description: The session's web-search budget (200 calls) was exhausted before planned queries on BIS CPMI Red Book coverage of non-member jurisdictions, EBRD Transition Report / Banking Environment and Performance Survey for MK, SeeNews and Seebiz regional coverage, Mastercard/Visa/Worldpay Global Payments Report MK entries, and Macedonian-language queries for archived tariff books ('архивиран тарифник', 'стара верзија тарифник').
negative_findings.result_summary: Several planned aggregator/archive avenues in this cell were never searched.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Coverage of this cell is good but not exhaustive; a follow-up run with fresh search budget should complete these branches before the cell is treated as closed.

negative_findings.description: Macedonian-language search was performed (one substantive Cyrillic query on analytical banking/payments studies for the Western Balkans and MK), but no Macedonian-language commercial aggregator, archive service or local analyst house was found. All aggregator-layer sources in this cell are English-language and foreign; the only MK-language hits were primary institutional sources (NBRSM, Ministry of Finance/UFR, bank product pages, Sitel news).
negative_findings.result_summary: The aggregator/archive layer for MK payments appears to have no domestic MK-language equivalent.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms that for this cell the local-language route leads back to primary sources (other cells' territory), and that the archive layer must carry the MK-language burden — Wayback snapshots of MK-language NBRSM and bank pages, which is why the CDX approach ranks critical here.

negative_findings.description: Two aggregators refused automated access during this run: ceicdata.com returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch (though a plain curl to the same URL returned 200), and thebanks.eu returned HTTP 403 to curl with a browser user-agent. fred.stlouisfed.org returned no response (code 000) to curl from this environment.
negative_findings.result_summary: Bot defences and environment-level connectivity, not dead links; all three should be treated as live-but-defended pending the deterministic verification pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Collection design for this cell must assume browser-grade fetching (or licensed APIs) for the commercial aggregator layer, not naive HTTP clients.

coverage_gaps.description: Card-scheme and payments-industry research (Visa, Mastercard, Worldpay/FIS Global Payments Report, Nilson Report, Euromonitor Consumer Finance) was not searched; these vendors publish MK or Southeast-Europe card-volume and payment-mix estimates that are the closest commercial analogue to official card statistics.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: In a follow-up run, query for 'Worldpay Global Payments Report North Macedonia', 'Mastercard Western Balkans cashless', 'Euromonitor consumer payments North Macedonia', and check whether any free country annex exists.

coverage_gaps.description: BIS CPMI Red Book / CPMI statistics and EBRD outputs (Transition Report, Banking Environment and Performance Survey) were not reached before the search budget ran out.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Search BIS CPMI statistics for any Western Balkans coverage and EBRD publications for MK financial-sector chapters; both are free and highly citable comparator sources.

coverage_gaps.description: The Wayback CDX enumeration was run only for nbrm.mk with a 'platni' filter and a 25-row limit. The same technique has not been applied to nbstat.nbrm.mk, stat.gov.mk, the nine MK commercial bank domains, KIBS (the domestic clearing house), or the MK card-scheme/processor sites, and no 'karti'/'tarif'/'statistik' filters were run against nbrm.mk itself.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a systematic CDX sweep over a defined MK domain list with filters on karti|tarif|statistik|platni|izvestaj|godisen, no row limit, collapse by digest, and store the full snapshot inventory as the archive backbone for the whole run.

coverage_gaps.description: Only the Internet Archive was used. Other preservation routes — archive.today/archive.ph, Common Crawl, Bing/Google cache, national or library web archives, and the EU/Europeana web-archiving initiatives — were not tested for MK banking pages.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Test archive.today and Common Crawl index lookups for nbrm.mk and MK bank domains; note that archive.today is aggressively bot-defended and may need manual access.

coverage_gaps.description: For every paid aggregator in this cell (CEIC, Trading Economics, Statista, Mordor/ResearchAndMarkets, bne IntelliNews, TheBanks.eu) it is unknown whether the organisation already holds a subscription, which determines whether these become collectable sources or stay reference-only.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish the existing subscription inventory before the collection routine is built, and mark collection_allowed accordingly; where no subscription exists, prefer the free substitutes identified here (DBnomics, World Bank API, IMF FAS, ECB Data Portal).

coverage_gaps.description: No comparator peer group has been fixed for MK. ECB PAY, World Bank and IMF FAS all allow arbitrary country selections, but without an agreed peer set (WB6 neighbours vs recent EU entrants vs euro-area small states) benchmark outputs will not be reproducible across runs.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Fix a standing comparator list (suggest: AL, RS, BA, ME, XK for regional; BG, RO, HR, GR, SI for EU/euro-adjacent) and hard-code it into every aggregator pull.

brief: For North Macedonia payments and card statistics, the aggregator layer splits cleanly into a free, API-addressable public tier (IMF Financial Access Survey and its FRED/DBnomics mirrors for ATM and POS counts, World Bank Open Data and Global Findex 2025 for density and demand-side cash/card behaviour, and the ECB Data Portal PAY dataset purely as an EU comparator since MK is not an ECB reporter) and a bot-defended commercial tier (CEIC, Trading Economics, Statista, TheBanks.eu, syndicated e-commerce vendors) whose MK content is largely modelled or re-derived and whose value is as a market-belief benchmark and pointer rather than as evidence. The archive layer is the strongest and most distinctive asset of this cell: a Wayback CDX query against nbrm.mk returned a rich inventory of superseded 'Годишна информација за движењата во плаќањата' annual payment reports (2017-2020) and Excel workbooks whose live URLs now redirect, 403 or 404 — making the Internet Archive the only practical route to MK historical payment series and withdrawn tariff books. Regional benchmarking is anchored by the World Bank / RCC / CEFTA Western Balkans Payments Modernization Project under the Common Regional Market agenda, with NBRSM's own Macedonian-language press confirming MK participation in the ECB and Banca d'Italia-supported regional interlinking work. Notably, no domestic Macedonian-language aggregator or archive service exists, no free aggregator was found carrying an MK POS-terminal series, and no primary rating-agency document on MK banks was publicly reachable — so the archive sweep plus NBRSM's PxWeb database should carry this cell's collection design.
